subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should non-owner, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns keep protected core tool schemas model-visible for cache stability when execution is denied before hooks and side effects?
rationale: Source inspection and tests can establish that calls are denied, but they cannot decide whether exposing protected tool names and schemas to unauthorized model turns is an acceptable permanent security and product boundary.

options.title: Accept stable visible schemas
options.body: Keep the stable catalogue and require the immutable execution-time gate across local tools, harnesses, and loopback MCP, followed by conflict-safe exact-head proof.

options.title: Preserve hidden schemas
options.body: Reject unauthorized schema visibility and redesign cache reuse around provider-specific prompt or continuation behavior without exposing protected definitions.

recommendation.title: Accept stable visible schemas
recommendation.body: Keep the stable catalogue and require the immutable execution-time gate across local tools, harnesses, and loopback MCP, followed by conflict-safe exact-head proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership of central embedded runtime and turn-setup behavior makes this the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting boundary choice.
